Param Vir Chakra: First recipient was Major Somnath Sharma (1947, 4 Kumaon Regiment)
Ashok Chakra is the highest peacetime military gallantry decoration in India
First Asian/Indian Nobel Laureate: Rabindranath Tagore (Literature, 1913, 'Gitanjali')
First Jnanpith Award winner: G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam, 1965); 1st woman: Ashapurna Devi (1976)
Dadasaheb Phalke Award: Highest honor in Indian cinema; first recipient was Devika Rani (1969)
Youngest Bharat Ratna recipient: Sachin Tendulkar (2014, age 40)

lessons.title: Important Days: National & International Observances, Historical Milestones & UN Themes

content_json.definition: Important Days and National/International Observances in competitive examinations (SSC CGL/CHSL, RRB NTPC, State PSCs, Banking, CDS, NDA) evaluate knowledge of critical milestone dates commemorating foundational historical events, scientific discoveries, constitutional adoption, global environmental consciousness, public health awareness, and United Nations socio-humanitarian declarations.
content_json.overview:
Calendar Categorization of Important Days:
- National Historical & Institutional Days: Commemorating Indian icons and institutional foundations (Army Day [Jan 15], National Voters' Day [Jan 25], National Science Day [Feb 28], National Technology Day [May 11], Kargil Vijay Diwas [Jul 26], National Sports Day [Aug 29], Rashtriya Ekta Diwas [Oct 31], Constitution Day [Nov 26], Good Governance Day [Dec 25])
- United Nations & Global Human Rights Days: Universal observances by UN agencies (International Women's Day [Mar 8], World Refugee Day [Jun 20], International Day of Peace [Sep 21], World Food Day [Oct 16], Human Rights Day [Dec 10])
- Environmental & Ecological Protection Sequence: World Wetlands Day [Feb 2], World Forest Day [Mar 21], World Water Day [Mar 22], World Earth Day [Apr 22], World Biodiversity Day [May 22], World Environment Day [Jun 5], World Ozone Day [Sep 16]
- Global Public Health & Epidemiology: World Cancer Day [Feb 4], World TB Day [Mar 24], World Health Day [Apr 7], World Malaria Day [Apr 25], World AIDS Day [Dec 1]
- Educational, Intellectual & Scientific Days: World IP Day [Apr 26], National Doctors' Day [Jul 1], National Teachers' Day [Sep 5], Engineers' Day [Sep 15], National Education Day [Nov 11], National Mathematics Day [Dec 22]

types.name: 1. National Milestone & Iconic Birth Observances
types.desc: Dates honoring great Indian leaders, freedom fighters, and constitutional milestones.
examples: Jan 12 (National Youth Day - Swami Vivekananda) • Jan 23 (Parakram Diwas - Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose)
Oct 31 (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas - Sardar Patel) • Dec 25 (Good Governance Day - Atal Bihari Vajpayee)

types.name: 2. UN & International Human Rights Commemorations
types.desc: Global days declared by the UN General Assembly to promote human rights and social justice.
examples: Mar 8 (International Women's Day) • May 1 (International Workers' Day / May Day)
Dec 10 (Human Rights Day - 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights)

types.name: 3. Environmental, Biodiversity & Earth Science Days
types.desc: Key ecological observances protecting oceans, atmosphere, water, and biosphere.
examples: Mar 22 (World Water Day) • Apr 22 (Earth Day) • May 22 (World Biodiversity Day)
Jun 5 (World Environment Day - Stockholm 1972) • Sep 16 (World Ozone Day - Montreal 1987)

types.name: 4. Public Health, Disease Awareness & Medical Days
types.desc: WHO-endorsed campaigns raising global awareness against epidemic diseases.
examples: Feb 4 (World Cancer Day) • Mar 24 (World TB Day - Robert Koch 1882)
Apr 7 (World Health Day - WHO founding 1948) • Dec 1 (World AIDS Day)

types.name: 5. Science, Technology, Innovation & Education Days
types.desc: Milestones commemorating scientific breakthroughs, engineers, and educational icons.
examples: Feb 28 (National Science Day - Raman Effect 1928) • May 11 (National Technology Day - Pokhran-II 1998)
Sep 15 (Engineers' Day - M. Visvesvaraya) • Dec 22 (National Mathematics Day - S. Ramanujan)

rules.title: The '22nd Day' Consecutive Eco-Sequence Rule
rules.explanation: Remember the three consecutive months falling on the 22nd day: March 22 = Water, April 22 = Earth, May 22 = Biodiversity.
rules.correct: March 22 is World Water Day; April 22 is World Earth Day; May 22 is International Day for Biological Diversity.
rules.incorrect: April 22 is World Water Day and March 22 is Earth Day.

rules.title: National vs. International Commemoration Pairs
rules.explanation: Differentiate national birth anniversaries from UN international observances: Jan 12 = National Youth Day vs Aug 12 = International Youth Day; Sep 5 = National Teachers' Day vs Oct 5 = World Teachers' Day.
rules.correct: National Youth Day is observed on January 12; International Youth Day is observed on August 12.
rules.incorrect: National Youth Day is celebrated on August 12.

rules.title: Scientific Discovery vs. Technology Milestone Rule
rules.explanation: February 28 marks Sir C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928 (National Science Day). May 11 marks the 1998 Pokhran-II nuclear tests (National Technology Day).
rules.correct: National Science Day (Feb 28) marks the Raman Effect discovery; National Technology Day (May 11) marks Pokhran-II.
rules.incorrect: National Science Day celebrates the birthday of C.V. Raman on February 28.

rules.title: Democratic & Constitutional Days Chronology
rules.explanation: January 25 is National Voters' Day (foundation of Election Commission in 1950); November 26 is Constitution Day (adoption of Constitution in 1949); April 24 is National Panchayati Raj Day (73rd Amendment enforcement in 1993).
rules.correct: November 26 is observed as Constitution Day commemorating the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1949.
rules.incorrect: November 26 is Republic Day celebrating the commencement of the Indian Constitution.

rules.title: Public Health Discovery & Foundation Rule
rules.explanation: World Health Day (April 7) marks the creation of the World Health Organization in 1948. World TB Day (March 24) marks Robert Koch's 1882 discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
rules.correct: April 7 is World Health Day marking the adoption of the WHO constitution in 1948.
rules.incorrect: World Health Day is observed on March 24.

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing National Youth Day with International Youth Day.
common_mistakes.correction: National Youth Day is January 12 (Swami Vivekananda); International Youth Day is August 12 (UN).
common_mistakes.rationale: Examiners routinely mix the two months (January vs August) to test candidate precision.

common_mistakes.mistake: Believing World Environment Day is celebrated on April 22.
common_mistakes.correction: April 22 is Earth Day; World Environment Day is June 5 (Stockholm Conference 1972).
common_mistakes.rationale: Candidates frequently mix up Earth Day (April 22) and Environment Day (June 5).

common_mistakes.mistake: Mixing up National Science Day with National Technology Day.
common_mistakes.correction: National Science Day is February 28 (Raman Effect 1928); National Technology Day is May 11 (Pokhran-II 1998).
common_mistakes.rationale: Pure scientific discovery vs. strategic technological defense achievement.

common_mistakes.mistake: Thinking National Voters' Day is January 26.
common_mistakes.correction: National Voters' Day is January 25, the day before Republic Day, marking the founding of the Election Commission of India.
common_mistakes.rationale: Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950.

quick_revision_points: January: 9th (Pravasi Bharatiya Divas), 12th (National Youth Day), 15th (Army Day), 23rd (Parakram Diwas), 24th (National Girl Child Day), 25th (National Voters' Day), 30th (Martyrs' Day).
February: 2nd (World Wetlands Day - Ramsar 1971), 4th (World Cancer Day), 13th (National Women's Day - Sarojini Naidu), 28th (National Science Day - Raman Effect 1928).
March: 8th (International Women's Day), 15th (World Consumer Rights Day), 21st (World Forestry Day), 22nd (World Water Day), 24th (World Tuberculosis Day).
April: 7th (World Health Day - WHO 1948), 22nd (Earth Day), 24th (National Panchayati Raj Day - 73rd Amendment 1993), 26th (World Intellectual Property Day).
May: 1st (International Workers' Day), 11th (National Technology Day - Pokhran-II 1998), 22nd (International Day for Biological Diversity), 31st (World No Tobacco Day).
June: 5th (World Environment Day - Stockholm 1972), 21st (International Day of Yoga - Summer Solstice).
July: 1st (National Doctors' Day - Dr. B.C. Roy & GST Day), 11th (World Population Day), 26th (Kargil Vijay Diwas - 1999), 29th (International Tiger Day).
August: 7th (National Handloom Day & National Javelin Day), 12th (International Youth Day), 23rd (National Space Day - Chandrayaan-3 landing 2023), 29th (National Sports Day - Dhyan Chand).
September: 5th (Teachers' Day - Dr. S. Radhakrishnan), 15th (Engineers' Day - Sir M. Visvesvaraya), 16th (World Ozone Day - Montreal Protocol 1987), 27th (World Tourism Day).
October: 2nd (International Day of Non-Violence - Mahatma Gandhi), 8th (Air Force Day), 16th (World Food Day - FAO 1945), 24th (United Nations Day - 1945), 31st (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas - Sardar Patel).
November: 11th (National Education Day - Maulana Azad), 14th (Children's Day & World Diabetes Day), 26th (Constitution Day - Samvidhan Divas).
December: 1st (World AIDS Day), 4th (Navy Day - Operation Trident 1971), 10th (Human Rights Day - UDHR 1948), 22nd (National Mathematics Day - Ramanujan), 25th (Good Governance Day - Vajpayee).

lessons.title: Books and Authors: Ancient Sanskrit Treatises, Medieval Chronicles, Freedom Struggle Literature & Contemporary Award Winners

content_json.definition: Books and Authors in competitive exams (UPSC CSE, SSC CGL/CHSL, CDS, NDA, State PSCs, Banking) evaluates literary heritage across chronological eras: ancient Sanskrit treatises on statecraft, astronomy, and classical drama; medieval Persian and vernacular court chronicles; freedom struggle autobiographies and philosophical treatises; and contemporary Booker, Jnanpith, and Sahitya Akademi award-winning literature.
content_json.overview:
Literary Heritage Classification:
- Ancient Sanskrit & Classical Literature: Statecraft (Kautilya's *Arthashastra*), Grammar (Panini's *Ashtadhyayi*, Patanjali's *Mahabhasya*), Classical Drama (Kalidasa's *Abhijnanasakuntalam*, *Meghaduta*; Vishakhadatta's *Mudrarakshasa*; Shudraka's *Mrichchhakatika*), Medicine (Charaka's *Charaka Samhita*, Sushruta's *Sushruta Samhita*), History (Kalhana's *Rajatarangini*)
- Medieval Chronicles & Court Memoirs: Al-Biruni (*Kitab-ul-Hind*), Babur (*Baburnama* in Chagatai Turkish), Gulbadan Begum (*Humayun-nama*), Abul Fazl (*Akbarnama*, *Ain-i-Akbari*), Jahangir (*Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri*), Abdul Hamid Lahori (*Padshahnama*)
- National Movement & Freedom Struggle Works: Dadabhai Naoroji (*Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*), Mahatma Gandhi (*The Story of My Experiments with Truth*, *Hind Swaraj*), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (*Gita Rahasya*), Jawaharlal Nehru (*The Discovery of India*, *Glimpses of World History*), Maulana Azad (*India Wins Freedom*), Dr. Rajendra Prasad (*India Divided*), Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (*The Annihilation of Caste*), Lala Lajpat Rai (*Unhappy India*)
- Post-Independence Classics: Rabindranath Tagore (*Gitanjali*, 1913 Nobel Prize), Munshi Premchand (*Godan*, *Gaban*, *Karmabhoomi*), R.K. Narayan (*Malgudi Days*, *The Guide*), Khushwant Singh (*Train to Pakistan*), Salman Rushdie (*Midnight's Children*), Vikram Seth (*A Suitable Boy*)
- Booker Prize & Global Laureates: Arundhati Roy (*The God of Small Things*, 1997), Kiran Desai (*The Inheritance of Loss*, 2006), Aravind Adiga (*The White Tiger*, 2008), Geetanjali Shree (*Tomb of Sand*, 2022 International Booker)

types.name: 1. Ancient Classical Treatises & Sanskrit Drama
types.desc: Foundational texts in polity, drama, medicine, and linguistics from antiquity.
examples: Kautilya (*Arthashastra* - statecraft) • Panini (*Ashtadhyayi* - grammar)
Kalidasa (*Abhijnanasakuntalam*) • Vishakhadatta (*Mudrarakshasa*) • Shudraka (*Mrichchhakatika*)

types.name: 2. Medieval Court Chronicles & Royal Memoirs
types.desc: Chronicles and autobiographical accounts composed during the Sultanate and Mughal periods.
examples: Babur (*Baburnama*) • Gulbadan Begum (*Humayun-nama*) • Abul Fazl (*Akbarnama*, *Ain-i-Akbari*)
Kalhana (*Rajatarangini* - history of Kashmir) • Al-Biruni (*Kitab-ul-Hind*)

types.name: 3. Nationalist Freedom Struggle Memoirs & Treatises
types.desc: Seminal political writings and prison autobiographies that shaped the Indian freedom movement.
examples: Dadabhai Naoroji (*Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*) • Gandhi (*Hind Swaraj*, *My Experiments with Truth*)
Nehru (*The Discovery of India*) • Tilak (*Gita Rahasya*) • Ambedkar (*Annihilation of Caste*)

types.name: 4. Modern Indian Classics & Vernacular Masterpieces
types.desc: Literary masterpieces capturing Indian social realities, partition, and identity.
examples: Rabindranath Tagore (*Gitanjali*, *Gora*) • Munshi Premchand (*Godan*, *Nirmala*)
R.K. Narayan (*Malgudi Days*, *The Guide*) • Khushwant Singh (*Train to Pakistan*)

types.name: 5. International Booker & Award-Winning Fiction
types.desc: Indian authors and diaspora writers honored with the Booker and international literary prizes.
examples: Arundhati Roy (*The God of Small Things*, 1997) • Kiran Desai (*The Inheritance of Loss*, 2006)
Aravind Adiga (*The White Tiger*, 2008) • Geetanjali Shree (*Tomb of Sand*, 2022 Int'l Booker)

rules.title: Ancient Sanskrit Playwright Association Rule
rules.explanation: Pair classical dramatists with their signature works: Kalidasa (*Abhijnanasakuntalam*), Vishakhadatta (*Mudrarakshasa*), Shudraka (*Mrichchhakatika*), Banabhatta (*Harshacharita*, *Kadambari*).
rules.correct: *Mudrarakshasa* was composed by Vishakhadatta; *Mrichchhakatika* was written by King Shudraka.
rules.incorrect: *Mudrarakshasa* was written by Kautilya or Kalidasa.

rules.title: Freedom Struggle Book Title Disambiguation Rule
rules.explanation: Carefully separate similarly titled freedom struggle works: Maulana Azad = *India Wins Freedom*; Dr. Rajendra Prasad = *India Divided*; Lala Lajpat Rai = *Unhappy India*; Dadabhai Naoroji = *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*.
rules.correct: *India Wins Freedom* is the autobiographical work of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; *India Divided* was written by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
rules.incorrect: *India Wins Freedom* was written by Jawaharlal Nehru or Rajendra Prasad.

rules.title: Mughal Memoir vs. Biography Authorship Rule
rules.explanation: Babur (*Baburnama*) and Jahangir (*Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri*) wrote their own autobiographies. Humayun's biography (*Humayun-nama*) was written by his sister Gulbadan Begum. Akbar's biography (*Akbarnama*) was written by Abul Fazl.
rules.correct: *Humayun-nama* was authored by Gulbadan Begum on the request of Emperor Akbar.
rules.incorrect: Humayun authored his own autobiography titled *Humayun-nama*.

rules.title: Booker Prize Indian Winners Chronology Rule
rules.explanation: Indian citizens/origin Booker winners: Salman Rushdie (1981 - *Midnight's Children*), Arundhati Roy (1997 - *The God of Small Things*), Kiran Desai (2006 - *The Inheritance of Loss*), Aravind Adiga (2008 - *The White Tiger*). Geetanjali Shree won International Booker (2022 - *Tomb of Sand*).
rules.correct: Arundhati Roy was the first Indian citizen to win the Man Booker Prize in 1997 for *The God of Small Things*.
rules.incorrect: Jhumpa Lahiri won the Man Booker Prize (she won the Pulitzer Prize for *Interpreter of Maladies*).

rules.title: Kashmir History & Early Chronicles Rule
rules.explanation: Kalhana's *Rajatarangini* (River of Kings, 1148-1150 CE) is India's first systematic Sanskrit historical chronicle recording the kings of Kashmir.
rules.correct: *Rajatarangini*, composed by Kalhana in Sanskrit verse, provides the history of Kashmir rulers.
rules.incorrect: *Rajatarangini* describes the history of Magadha or the Gupta empire.

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing 'India Divided' with 'India Wins Freedom'.
common_mistakes.correction: 'India Divided' was written by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, while 'India Wins Freedom' was written by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
common_mistakes.rationale: Both were top leaders who authored seminal analyses during the partition era.

common_mistakes.mistake: Thinking Chanakya wrote the play 'Mudrarakshasa'.
common_mistakes.correction: Chanakya (Kautilya) is the central character, but the playwright was Vishakhadatta.
common_mistakes.rationale: Candidates confuse the historical hero of the drama with its author.

common_mistakes.mistake: Believing Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize for the novel 'Gora'.
common_mistakes.correction: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his poetry collection 'Gitanjali'.
common_mistakes.rationale: 'Gora' is an acclaimed novel by Tagore, but the Nobel Prize was specifically awarded for 'Gitanjali'.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming 'Anandamath' was written by Rabindranath Tagore.
common_mistakes.correction: 'Anandamath' was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1882, which introduced India's national song 'Vande Mataram'.
common_mistakes.rationale: Tagore composed 'Jana Gana Mana' while Bankim Chandra composed 'Vande Mataram'.

quick_revision_points: Kautilya (Chanakya): *Arthashastra* (ancient treatise on statecraft, espionage, military strategy, and public finance).
Kalidasa: *Abhijnanasakuntalam*, *Meghaduta*, *Raghuvamsha*, *Kumarasambhava*, *Malavikagnimitram*.
Vishakhadatta: *Mudrarakshasa* (play on Chandragupta Maurya and Chanakya) and *Devichandraguptam*.
Shudraka: *Mrichchhakatika* (The Little Clay Cart) | Harsha: *Ratnavali*, *Priyadarsika*, *Nagananda*.
Banabhatta: *Harshacharita* (biography of King Harshavardhana) and *Kadambari*.
Kalhana: *Rajatarangini* (verse chronicle of Kashmiri kings written in 1148-1150 CE).
Panini: *Ashtadhyayi* (Sanskrit grammar) | Patanjali: *Mahabhasya* (commentary on Panini).
Abul Fazl: *Akbarnama* and *Ain-i-Akbari* | Gulbadan Begum: *Humayun-nama*.
Babur: *Baburnama* (Tuzuk-i-Baburi in Chagatai Turkish) | Jahangir: *Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri* in Persian.
Dadabhai Naoroji: *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* (1901 - Drain of Wealth theory).
Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay: *Anandamath* (source of 'Vande Mataram'), *Durgeshnandini*, *Kapalkundala*.
Mahatma Gandhi: *The Story of My Experiments with Truth*, *Hind Swaraj* (1909), *Key to Health*.
Jawaharlal Nehru: *The Discovery of India*, *Glimpses of World History*, *An Autobiography* (Toward Freedom).
Bal Gangadhar Tilak: *Gita Rahasya* (written in Mandalay jail) and *The Arctic Home in the Vedas*.
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad: *India Wins Freedom*, *Ghubar-i-Khatir* | Dr. Rajendra Prasad: *India Divided*.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar: *The Annihilation of Caste*, *The Buddha and His Dhamma*, *Who Were the Shudras?*.
Lala Lajpat Rai: *Unhappy India*, *Young India* | Sarojini Naidu: *The Golden Threshold*, *The Broken Wing*.
Rabindranath Tagore: *Gitanjali* (1913 Nobel Prize), *Gora*, *Ghare Baire* (The Home and the World).
Munshi Premchand: *Godan*, *Gaban*, *Karmabhoomi*, *Nirmala*, *Idgah*, *Kafan*.
R.K. Narayan: *Swami and Friends*, *The Guide*, *Malgudi Days*, *The English Teacher*.

Booker Prize Winners: Arundhati Roy (*The God of Small Things*, 1997), Kiran Desai (*The Inheritance of Loss*, 2006), Aravind Adiga (*The White Tiger*, 2008), Geetanjali Shree (*Tomb of Sand*, 2022 Int'l Booker).

lessons.title: Sports: Tournaments, Grand Slams, Domestic Cups, Olympic Records & National Sports Awards

content_json.definition: Sports General Knowledge in competitive examinations (SSC CGL/CHSL, RRB NTPC, State PSCs, CDS, Banking) encompasses major multi-sport global events (Olympics, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games), international federation championships (ICC Cricket World Cups, FIFA World Cup, Badminton Thomas & Uber Cups, Tennis Grand Slams), historic domestic trophies, sports terminology, and premier national athletic honors.
content_json.overview:
Comprehensive Sports GK Framework:
- Olympic Games & Indian Milestones: First modern Olympics (Athens 1896); First Indian individual medalist (K.D. Jadhav - Bronze in Wrestling, Helsinki 1952); First Indian woman medalist (Karnam Malleswari - Bronze in Weightlifting, Sydney 2000); First individual Gold (Abhinav Bindra - 10m Air Rifle, Beijing 2008); First athletics Gold (Neeraj Chopra - Javelin 87.58m, Tokyo 2020)
- Grand Slam Tennis Calendar & Surfaces: Chronological sequence -> Australian Open (Jan, Hard/Plexicushion) -> French Open / Roland Garros (May-Jun, Red Clay) -> Wimbledon (Jun-Jul, Perennial Ryegrass) -> US Open (Aug-Sep, Hard/DecoTurf)
- Cricket Milestones & Domestic Cups: India World Cup victories (1983 ODI - Kapil Dev, 2011 ODI - M.S. Dhoni, 2007 T20 - M.S. Dhoni, 2024 T20 - Rohit Sharma); Domestic trophies: Ranji Trophy (first-class, 1934), Duleep Trophy, Irani Cup, Vijay Hazare Trophy (List A 50-over), Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20)
- Football Cups: Durand Cup (Shimla 1888 - oldest in Asia, 3rd oldest globally), Santosh Trophy (Inter-state national championship), Rover's Cup, IFA Shield
- Hockey Trophies: Beighton Cup (Kolkata 1895 - oldest hockey tournament), Aga Khan Cup, Rangaswami Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy
- Badminton Team Cups: Thomas Cup (Men's world team championship - India won maiden title in 2022 defeating Indonesia 3-0), Uber Cup (Women's world team championship), Sudirman Cup (Mixed team)
- National Sports Awards (Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports): Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (highest honor, Rs. 25 lakh; first recipient Viswanathan Anand 1991-92), Arjuna Award (Rs. 15 lakh, 4 years outstanding consistency), Dronacharya Award (coaches, Rs. 15 lakh lifetime / Rs. 10 lakh regular), Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy (top performing university)

types.name: 1. Olympic Games & Indian Athletic Milestones
types.desc: Olympic history, host cities, and groundbreaking Indian medalists.
examples: K.D. Jadhav (1952 Bronze Wrestling) • Karnam Malleswari (2000 Bronze Weightlifting)
Abhinav Bindra (2008 Gold Shooting) • Neeraj Chopra (2020 Gold Javelin 87.58m)

types.name: 2. Grand Slam Tennis Architecture & Surfaces
types.desc: The four annual tennis majors in chronological order and their court characteristics.
examples: Australian Open (Hard) • French Open / Roland Garros (Red Clay)
Wimbledon (Grass - oldest, 1877) • US Open (Hard)

types.name: 3. Indian Domestic Trophies Multi-Sport Classification
types.desc: Historic domestic competitions across cricket, football, hockey, and golf.
examples: Cricket: Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy, Irani Cup
Football: Durand Cup (1888), Santosh Trophy • Hockey: Beighton Cup (1895), Aga Khan Cup

types.name: 4. Badminton & Racket Sports World Cups
types.desc: Men's, women's, and mixed world team championships.
examples: Thomas Cup: Men's Badminton (India won maiden title in 2022 defeating Indonesia 3-0)
Uber Cup: Women's Badminton • Sudirman Cup: Mixed Team Badminton • Davis Cup: Men's Tennis

types.name: 5. National Sports Awards & Financial Incentives
types.desc: National athletic honors conferred by the President of India on National Sports Day (Aug 29).
examples: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna: Rs. 25 Lakh (highest award; first winner Viswanathan Anand)
Arjuna Award: Rs. 15 Lakh • Dronacharya Award: Rs. 15 Lakh (Lifetime) / Rs. 10 Lakh (Regular)

rules.title: Grand Slam Chronological Order & Surfaces Rule
rules.explanation: Remember the acronym 'AFWU': Australian Open (Hard) -> French Open (Red Clay) -> Wimbledon (Grass) -> US Open (Hard).
rules.correct: The French Open is played on red clay courts; Wimbledon is played on natural grass courts.
rules.incorrect: Wimbledon is played on hard synthetic acrylic courts.

rules.title: Domestic Cup Multi-Sport Association Rule
rules.explanation: Durand Cup and Santosh Trophy are Football tournaments; Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy are Cricket tournaments; Beighton Cup and Aga Khan Cup are Hockey tournaments.
rules.correct: The Durand Cup, founded in 1888, is the oldest football tournament in Asia.
rules.incorrect: The Durand Cup is a cricket or polo tournament.

rules.title: Pioneering Indian Olympic Medalists Chronology Rule
rules.explanation: K.D. Jadhav = 1952 (first individual medal - Bronze); Karnam Malleswari = 2000 (first woman medal - Bronze); Abhinav Bindra = 2008 (first individual Gold); Neeraj Chopra = 2020 (first athletics Gold).
rules.correct: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in the men's 10m air rifle at Beijing 2008.
rules.incorrect: Neeraj Chopra was India's first individual Olympic gold medalist.

rules.title: Badminton Cup Gender Distinction Rule
rules.explanation: Thomas Cup is the world men's team badminton championship; Uber Cup is the world women's team badminton championship. Remember 'T' for Thomas = Men, 'U' for Uber = Women.
rules.correct: India won the men's world team championship (Thomas Cup) in 2022 by defeating Indonesia.
rules.incorrect: India won the Uber Cup in 2022.

rules.title: National Sports Awards Post-2020 Revision Rule
rules.explanation: Following the August 2020 revision: Khel Ratna = Rs. 25 lakh; Arjuna Award = Rs. 15 lakh; Dronacharya (Lifetime) = Rs. 15 lakh; Dronacharya (Regular) = Rs. 10 lakh.
rules.correct: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award carries a cash prize of Rs. 25 lakh.
rules.incorrect: The Khel Ratna Award carries a prize of Rs. 7.5 lakh (that was the old pre-2020 prize).

common_mistakes.mistake: Thinking Milkha Singh won an Olympic bronze medal in 1960.
common_mistakes.correction: Milkha Singh finished fourth in the 400m final at the 1960 Rome Olympics, narrowly missing bronze by 0.1 seconds.
common_mistakes.rationale: Candidates confuse his celebrated Asian and Commonwealth Games gold medals with an Olympic medal.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming Thomas Cup is played for Tennis.
common_mistakes.correction: Thomas Cup is the premier men's world team championship in Badminton; Davis Cup is for men's Tennis.
common_mistakes.rationale: Both are prestigious men's team cups in racket sports, leading to frequent confusion.

common_mistakes.mistake: Believing the Durand Cup is a cricket trophy.
common_mistakes.correction: The Durand Cup is a historic football tournament, founded in 1888 in Shimla.
common_mistakes.rationale: Ranji Trophy is the premier domestic cricket trophy; Durand Cup is football.

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing the first woman Olympic medalist for India.
common_mistakes.correction: Karnam Malleswari won bronze in weightlifting at Sydney 2000; Mary Kom, Saina Nehwal, and P.V. Sindhu won in later Olympics.
common_mistakes.rationale: Chronological precedence: Malleswari (2000) was first, followed by Saina Nehwal and Mary Kom (2012 London).

quick_revision_points: Modern Olympic Games: First edition held in 1896 in Athens, Greece, founded by Baron Pierre de Coubertin.
First Indian individual Olympic medalist: Khashaba Dadasaheb (K.D.) Jadhav (Bronze in Bantamweight Wrestling, 1952 Helsinki).
First Indian woman Olympic medalist: Karnam Malleswari (Bronze in 69kg Weightlifting, 2000 Sydney).
First Indian individual Olympic Gold: Abhinav Bindra (10m Air Rifle Shooting, 2008 Beijing).
First Indian Athletics Olympic Gold: Neeraj Chopra (Men's Javelin Throw with 87.58m, 2020 Tokyo).
Grand Slam Tennis sequence: Australian Open (Hard) -> French Open (Clay) -> Wimbledon (Grass) -> US Open (Hard).
Cricket World Cup: India won in 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (M.S. Dhoni) in ODI format; 2007 (M.S. Dhoni) and 2024 (Rohit Sharma) in T20I format.
Domestic Cricket Trophies: Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Irani Cup, Vijay Hazare Trophy (One Day), Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20).
Domestic Football Trophies: Durand Cup (oldest in Asia, 1888), Santosh Trophy, Rover's Cup, IFA Shield.
Domestic Hockey Trophies: Beighton Cup (Kolkata, 1895 - oldest hockey tourney in India), Aga Khan Cup, Rangaswami Cup.
Badminton World Team Championships: Thomas Cup (Men), Uber Cup (Women), Sudirman Cup (Mixed Team). India won Thomas Cup in 2022.
Tennis Team Championships: Davis Cup (Men's international team event), Billie Jean King Cup (Women's team event).
National Sports Awards: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (Rs. 25 lakh, first winner Viswanathan Anand 1991-92).
Arjuna Award: Instituted in 1961 (Rs. 15 lakh prize) for consistently outstanding athletic performance over 4 years.
Dronacharya Award: Instituted in 1985 for sports coaches (Regular: Rs. 10 lakh; Lifetime: Rs. 15 lakh).
National Sports Day: Celebrated on August 29 marking the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand (The Hockey Wizard).

lessons.title: Current Affairs: Flagship Government Schemes, Space & Defense Missions, Multilateral Summits & Global Indices

content_json.definition: Current Affairs in competitive examinations (UPSC CSE, CDS, NDA, SSC CGL/CHSL, Banking/IBPS PO, State PSCs) evaluates contemporary national and global developments: flagship central welfare programs, space exploration and deep-tech missions (ISRO/DRDO), multilateral summits (G20, BRICS, SCO, COP), bilateral military exercises, and global institutional indices.
content_json.overview:
Major Current Affairs Domains:
- Flagship Central Government Welfare Schemes: PM-KISAN (Rs. 6,000/year in 3 installments of Rs. 2,000 via DBT; 100% Central Sector Scheme); Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (Rs. 5 lakh hospitalization cover per family per year); Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY - financial inclusion, zero-balance bank accounts, RuPay cards); Jal Jeevan Mission (55 lpcd tap water to every rural home); PM Vishwakarma (support for traditional artisans)
- ISRO Space Missions & Indigenous Defense: Chandrayaan-3 (landed on Moon's south polar region on August 23, 2023 via LVM3-M4; August 23 is National Space Day; landing site named 'Shiv Shakti Point'); Aditya-L1 (solar observatory at Lagrange Point 1 via PSLV-C57); Gaganyaan (crewed orbital flight demonstration); DRDO missile defense (Agni-V, BrahMos, Akash-NG)
- Multilateral Summits & Global Groupings: 18th G20 Summit (2023 New Delhi, Bharat Mandapam; theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' / 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'; African Union inducted as permanent member); BRICS expansion (Johannesburg summit); SCO expansion (Iran 2023, Belarus 2024); Quad (India, US, Japan, Australia)
- Bilateral Military, Naval & Air Drills: Army: Surya Kiran (Nepal), Yudh Abhyas & Vajra Prahar (USA), Sampriti (Bangladesh), Mitra Shakti (Sri Lanka), Nomadic Elephant (Mongolia); Navy: Varuna (France), Malabar (Quad), SIMBEX (Singapore), SLINEX (Sri Lanka); Air: Garuda (France), Tarang Shakti (multilateral)
- Global Indices & Publishing Bodies: Human Development Index (UNDP), World Economic Outlook (IMF), Global Gender Gap (WEF), Global Hunger Index (Concern Worldwide & Welthungerhilfe), Corruption Perceptions Index (Transparency International)

types.name: 1. Flagship Government Schemes & DBT Programs
types.desc: Key welfare initiatives, funding models, eligibility, and quantifiable entitlements.
examples: PM-KISAN: Rs. 6,000 per year in three 4-monthly installments of Rs. 2,000 via DBT
PM-JAY: Health insurance cover up to Rs. 5 Lakh per family per year for secondary/tertiary care

types.name: 2. ISRO Space Exploration & Scientific Missions
types.desc: Lunar, solar, and deep-space missions, launch vehicles, and national milestones.
examples: Chandrayaan-3: Soft-landed near lunar south pole on Aug 23, 2023 via LVM3-M4 ('Shiv Shakti Point')
Aditya-L1: Solar observatory positioned in halo orbit around Lagrange Point 1 (L1)

types.name: 3. Multilateral Summits & Geopolitical Groupings
types.desc: International alliances, rotating presidencies, summits, and institutional expansions.
examples: G20 2023: 18th Summit held in New Delhi; African Union inducted as permanent member
BRICS & SCO: Expansion to include new geopolitical partners (Iran, Egypt, UAE, etc.)

types.name: 4. Bilateral Military, Naval & Air Drills
types.desc: Interoperability defense exercises between Indian armed forces and foreign partners.
examples: Surya Kiran (India-Nepal Army) • Sampriti (India-Bangladesh Army) • Yudh Abhyas (India-USA)
Varuna (India-France Navy) • Malabar (Quad Navies: India, USA, Japan, Australia)

types.name: 5. Global Socio-Economic Indices & Publishing Bodies
types.desc: International ranking reports, publishing multilateral organizations, and evaluation dimensions.
examples: Human Development Index (HDI): Published by UNDP (health, education, standard of living)
Global Gender Gap: Published by World Economic Forum (WEF)

rules.title: Central Sector vs. Centrally Sponsored Funding Rule
rules.explanation: Central Sector Schemes are 100% funded and executed directly by the Union Government (e.g., PM-KISAN). Centrally Sponsored Schemes have a shared cost ratio between Centre and States (e.g., 60:40 or 90:10, like Jal Jeevan Mission).
rules.correct: PM-KISAN is a 100% Central Sector Scheme fully funded by the Central Government.
rules.incorrect: PM-KISAN funding is split 50:50 between the central government and state governments.

rules.title: ISRO Launch Vehicle Payload Distinctions Rule
rules.explanation: PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle - 4-stage rocket) vs. LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark 3 - 3-stage heavy lift rocket with cryogenic C25 stage for heavy payloads and lunar modules).
rules.correct: Chandrayaan-3 was launched using the LVM3-M4 rocket; Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57.
rules.incorrect: Chandrayaan-3 was launched aboard PSLV-C57.

rules.title: Defense Exercise Nomenclature & Service Wings Rule
rules.explanation: Differentiate French bilateral exercises: Shakti (Army), Varuna (Navy), Garuda (Air Force). Do not confuse Garuda (India-France Air) with Garuda Shakti (India-Indonesia Army).
rules.correct: Varuna is the bilateral naval exercise conducted between the navies of India and France.
rules.incorrect: Varuna is an army exercise between India and Russia.

rules.title: Multilateral Summit Presidencies & Themes Rule
rules.explanation: Presidencies rotate annually: G20 India (2023) -> Brazil (2024) -> South Africa (2025). India's 2023 theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future) from Maha Upanishad.
rules.correct: India held the G20 Presidency from December 1, 2022 to November 30, 2023, concluding with the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration.
rules.incorrect: India hosted the G20 summit in 2024.

rules.title: National Space Day & Landing Coordinates Rule
rules.explanation: August 23 is celebrated as 'National Space Day' to commemorate Chandrayaan-3's lunar soft landing. The touchdown site is named 'Shiv Shakti Point', and Chandrayaan-2's impact site is named 'Tiranga Point'.
rules.correct: The touchdown site of Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander on the Moon is named 'Shiv Shakti Point'.
rules.incorrect: The landing site of Chandrayaan-3 is named Tiranga Point (Tiranga Point is Chandrayaan-2's crash site).

common_mistakes.mistake: Thinking PM-KISAN is available only to small and marginal farmers.
common_mistakes.correction: When launched in Feb 2019, it was for small and marginal farmers (<2 hectares), but in May 2019 it was extended to all landholding farmer families.
common_mistakes.rationale: Exam questions test updated eligibility criteria versus original launch limitations.

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing Chandrayaan-3's launch vehicle with PSLV.
common_mistakes.correction: Chandrayaan-3 was launched aboard LVM3-M4 (heavy lift); Aditya-L1 was launched aboard PSLV-C57.
common_mistakes.rationale: ISRO uses different launch vehicles depending on the payload mass and target orbital trajectory.

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing Exercise 'Mitra Shakti' with 'Garuda Shakti'.
common_mistakes.correction: 'Mitra Shakti' is between India and Sri Lanka; 'Garuda Shakti' is between India and Indonesia.
common_mistakes.rationale: Both contain 'Shakti' in their operational code names.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming the Human Development Index is published by the World Bank.
common_mistakes.correction: HDI is published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP); the World Bank publishes the World Development Report.
common_mistakes.rationale: Candidates frequently mix up international financial institutions and UN agencies.

quick_revision_points: Chandrayaan-3: Launched on July 14, 2023, soft-landed near the Lunar South Pole on August 23, 2023. August 23 is declared National Space Day.
Landing point names: Chandrayaan-3 landing site = 'Shiv Shakti Point'; Chandrayaan-2 crash site = 'Tiranga Point'.
Aditya-L1: India's first solar space observatory, placed in halo orbit around Lagrange Point 1 (L1), launched by PSLV-C57.
18th G20 Summit (2023): Hosted at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. African Union inducted as permanent member. Theme: 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'.
PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi): Rs. 6,000/year in 3 equal installments of Rs. 2,000 via DBT. 100% Central Sector Scheme.
Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY): World's largest health assurance scheme providing Rs. 5 lakh cover per family per year for secondary/tertiary hospitalization.
PM Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY): National Mission on Financial Inclusion, launched on August 28, 2014, providing zero-balance bank accounts with RuPay debit cards.
Jal Jeevan Mission: Aims to provide functional household tap connections (FHTC) of 55 liters per capita per day to every rural household by Ministry of Jal Shakti.

Military Exercises: Surya Kiran (Nepal), Yudh Abhyas & Vajra Prahar (USA), Sampriti (Bangladesh), Mitra Shakti (Sri Lanka), Nomadic Elephant (Mongolia).
Naval Exercises: Malabar (Quad: India, US, Japan, Australia), Varuna (France), SIMBEX (Singapore), SLINEX (Sri Lanka), JIMEX (Japan).
